item.title: error handling, revisited
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I keep coming back to error handling, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Error handling shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: a short note about error handling
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
A quick write-up on error handling, mostly so future me stops relearning it.

why it matters

Error handling shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: thinking about error handling
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Short post: error handling is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Error handling shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
